episodes.title: The SEMA Show has changed over the years…
Conor Shanahan

moments.quote: there's no way that you could tell me that 2018 James Dean would absolutely destroy 2026. James, it's not possible. Yeah. And that's what I think a lot of people look up to James for is that like, he came back and like James is drifting quite a long time now and he's came. He's from, if you were to go back 12, 13 years ago and take a driver who retired and, and say, come back to drifting now. They wouldn't, I personally believe that they would struggle massively, but how much the sport has changed. I think Digo Saito is a great example that like,
moments.why: Gekozen door Joshua op het dashboard

moments.topic: THE TROPHY FLEW HOME IN A DRINKS CABINET
moments.quote: I got to ask about the logistics of bringing that trophy home. Like, did you end up booking a separate seat or like, did you have to keep it on your lap for the whole time or how did that all work out? Yeah, it was quite funny. Actually, the airline that we fly with to California is an Irish airline, Erlingus. Erlingus, yeah. So they're like really supportive, quite cool to, you know, ...
moments.why: Light, funny story about flying the 2026 FD trophy home to Ireland. Easy share.

moments.quote: To bring it home is always quite special. And yeah, I think I'm kind of a guy who like loves the small moments, you know, like it's always nice to come home and, you know, put it on the kitchen table for the first time. And I think when my mom will not take it off the kitchen table for at least probably two months. So that's kind of the rule. If we have a big win, they stay down there. ...
moments.why: Sweet family detail: big wins stay on the kitchen table for two months.

moments.topic: ONE HAND ON THE TITLE, NOT BOTH
moments.quote: Yeah, I'm also a big believer in that it's not over until it's in my hand, you know, and that's kind of yeah, I guess the break between Vegas and Long Beach was quite rough because it's I have one hand on it, but not both. You know, it's very close to being done and but still anything going to happen. I think that's what added so much pressure to the battle. Everyone's like, oh, it's just a top pretty too. But I'm like, yeah, but if I lose this top, or two, Jack or James going to win the event. So I'm not going to be champion.
moments.why: How the pressure felt between Vegas and Long Beach; fans remember that final.

moments.topic: "HE WAS GOING TO BE AN FD CHAMPION"
moments.quote: we all know that here, but I was going to be an FT champion, right? Like, yeah, I think, I think that's a foregone conclusion to be honest. Yeah. So I think like it's in Jerry's point of view, like he worked hard with that kid, the hero worked hard and I felt like he was maybe the last shot was took away from a little bit. So I'm like happy that, you know, you know, hero is such a good ...
moments.why: Conor zegt dat Hiroya Minowa een zekere toekomstige FD-kampioen was voordat hij naar rally ging.

moments.topic: COULD HIROYA MINOWA RACE A US RALLY?
moments.quote: Yeah. Yeah. It's, it's tough to see him step away into rally. And, but at the same time, like it looks like he's doing well there. I have a very strong feeling. We're going to see him climb the ranks of, of rally very soon, which might be very, which could be cool. Cause they're going to have around in the U S next year. So like the chance, there is a chance we might be able to see him ...
moments.why: Speculatie dat Hiroya Minowa volgend jaar een Amerikaanse rallyronde rijdt. Gerucht, gaat naar Joshua.

moments.topic: "YOU DRIVE HOW THE JUDGES TELL YOU"
moments.quote: you know, like, you know, the argument of people saying, Oh, you can't drive how you want to drive in competition. Well, no shit, you know, like, yeah, yeah, exactly. You know, you're going to drive. Yeah, I don't really understand that point. But yeah, of course, like we all critique stuff. We all maybe want stuff to be a little bit different. I think, you know, drifting is involving as a whole when it comes to our rule book and a judging rule book. But I don't get that sometimes, you know, I don't get that point of like, Oh, like, you know, competition driving, you don't drive how you want to drive. But like, that's kind of the whole point, right? Like you go to a room in the morning tree, guys tell you what to do. And you do that job the best you can, and you're going to win the you know, that's kind of my opinion how it works.
moments.why: Strong opinion on the 'you can't drive how you want' debate. Comment bait.

moments.quote: You need real people around you. You don't need people around you that are telling you like, Oh, well you've done good. You know, you lost the battle, but you almost had them. Like that's the part for me. When somebody says to me, I almost had you. I'm like, but you didn't. Yeah. That's the difference. Yeah. Almost had like, I would never, I hate that work being honest. There's one thing what annoys me in drifting when somebody says, Oh, but we almost had you, but you didn't. Yeah. You weren't good enough to have me. So go back and be realistic about that.
moments.why: Blunt quote, very shareable.

moments.topic: HIS SPOTTER WATCHES DRIFT EVENTS IN EGYPT
moments.quote: I said at the banquet, like, I would often text him late at night. And I'm like, what are you doing? He's like, I'm just watching a drift event. And I'm like, where's the drift event? And it's in like Egypt or something. And I'm like, you know, and I love drifting also. And I always felt for a while that I would never meet somebody who loved drifting just as much as me. But I definitely ...
moments.why: Funny detail about how obsessed his spotter Matt is. Name spelling: check.

moments.quote: me and Matt have a very simple number system, what we use. So like in battle situations, like a lot of the time, so Matt will give me a rundown before the battle, what I'm warming the towers up, what to expect, what to approach. But after that, it's very, it's very simple communication. We have a number system that we've studied very to a very high level. You maybe will see me do ...
moments.why: He and his spotter use a number system; slow practice runs are them practising it.

moments.topic: "IF IT FAILS, MY AMERICAN JOURNEY IS OVER"
moments.quote: You know, I talked about a lot about this journey year that in first 15 minutes, I knew that we were going to fight for a championship. That's very true. Like, that's not a saying that I just came up with that actually happened. And it wasn't that the car was that good. I didn't even drive the car at this point. But jury and his team gave me a sense of like, this is where I meant to be ...
moments.why: Strongest story of the episode: all-in bet on Jerry Yang's team.

moments.topic: "JAMES BEATING US WAS THE BEST THING"
moments.quote: we're like, I think we can get back to a good position. Do I think that we can fight for championship? Maybe not. You know, for sure, it wasn't a perfect year. There was still some things what could have been better on my side. And, you know, we had a little bit of bad look. But like, overall, when I look back at the year, I think it was everything what it needed to be. James whooped ...
moments.why: Says losing to James Deane in Orlando turned the season.

moments.topic: HIS CREW CHIEF DOES THE TESTING
moments.quote: Eric, my crew guy, holy shit, he can drive. Like, I actually really want to drive with him. I have watched a lot of these videos and stuff. And like, so anytime the car needed to get tested when I wasn't there, Eric was the one who done the testing on my car as well. Which I thought was sick. Like, there's not many teams can say that their crew chief guy was the guy who was driving it ...
moments.why: Little-known fact: crew chief Eric tests the car when Conor is in Europe.

moments.topic: 1,500 WHP AND NO NOS ALL YEAR
moments.quote: Even in Europe, there was a long time that I used like a smaller turbo than Jack. Right. So the VR suits my style, but then the VR went to the other extreme where we had a problem that it just was too much. Like the engine was too much. Like I was constantly asking to turn it down, turn it down, turn it down, turn it down. To the point that we almost couldn't turn it down anymore. First ...
moments.why: Big numbers and a surprising choice: he asked to turn the engine DOWN.

moments.quote: I was always like, oh, there's a way that we can make run -up better. There has got to be a way to like chasing on the run -up has to be better. So I started left foot braking always on the run -up, on the chase. So I would left foot brake to flick, like mimic the speed. Um, if there, even in Poland and my onboards and stuff, like Dylan Hughes asked me in FD, he was like, that blows my ...
moments.why: Claims he started left-foot braking on the chase run-up and others copied it (mentions Dylan Hughes and LZ). Check names.

moments.quote: There is not much of an off season actually. Um, yeah, I go to Japan next week to do D1, which I'm excited about. Um, yeah, so I got to go there and then I will go to Cyprus, which is kind of like a traditional trip. What Irish drivers do at the end of the year. I haven't went actually in the last three years, so I'm excited to go there. Um, and then I do a rally, which is kind of like ...
moments.why: D1 in Japan, Cyprus, a rally and Oman. Note: recorded right after Long Beach, so 'next week' may be past.

moments.topic: "THE BEST VERSION EVER OF CONOR SHANAHAN"
moments.quote: I really have a goal right now that I probably shouldn't say this, but I really have a goal that I want next year to be the best version ever of Connor Shanahan. And I mean that in many ways, like not just in the car. I mean, like, I really want to spend time working on myself and I want to somewhat take my health more serious towards drifting. I want to try focus more on kind of ...
moments.why: Plans for 2027: more fitness and preparation.

moments.topic: BIG FD CHANGES COMING NEXT YEAR?
moments.quote: Yeah. Yeah. I, next year I'm very, very excited for, I know it looks like there's going to be some changes as well, which is, is kind of cool. I don't know if you got that, the memo about. A lot of changes, I think. Yeah. And I think there's going to be more than even you and I don't have preview too. Like, it's, I know, I'm very excited to see what ends up happening next year with, ...
moments.why: Host and Conor hint at changes for next season they cannot share yet. Rumor, needs Joshua.

moments.quote: And I just want to take this opportunity to say thank you to them as well. And the people who hate me. Thank you so much because you guys motivate me more than ever as well. And keep hating me, please. I don't think there's many, but I'm sure there's some. I'm for sure. I think it's normal when you do something good. Yeah. Yeah. It's a, if somebody's pissed off with where you're going, ...
moments.why: Fun closing line to the haters.

moments.quote: But as far as competition goes, it stops here for Ryan Turk. Ryan Turk, the rock star energy drink driver, drifter, ripper, and gripper. Liffrier died at the motto of his home state, and that's how he lived. It's on his chest, it's on his brothers, it's on his dad's, and that is the motto of his state and the motto is hard. Father, husband, and friend to many, inspiration for a lot of automotive enthusiasts, not just a drifter, but just an absolute gentleman of a human being. moments.topic: WHY FD IS SO HARD TO WIN
moments.quote: Like no one just becomes a champion without working hard. Like F.D. is probably one of the hardest motorsport championships to win because like you can have the best team in road racing and be a decent driver and keep all four tires on the ground and win a championship road racing. Yeah, it is not like that drifting at all, because you can make a mistake every lap and still win road racing. Yeah, you cannot do that in drifting unless the other guy you're battling does it, too. Yeah. You almost can't make a mistake in a weekend. Like you got to go all the way. And like, you know, usually you make one or two and hopefully the other guy does, too. And then you got to beat the three guys up top that are deciding who wins. Right. Right. Understand what they want. Yeah. Because I'm not fighting for a lap time. Yeah. I'm fighting for a I win or lose.

moments.quote: Like it's like to me, it's very clear. Like I don't think there's to me, there's always a vast difference. That's what I believe. The problem with F.D. is right now, because the guy with 50 degrees angle did everything great and he did everything he was supposed to. OK. Driving at 62 degrees angle versus 50 is five times harder. Right. Should be that other run should be a 65 and that's a 95.
moments.why: Same run at 62 degrees vs 50 gets the same score now; he says it should be 95 vs 65.

moments.quote: And I think it's just because like all those dudes, I've watched James and Connor and Vaughn and like all these guys go drive fun events. And you're like, these dudes are insane. But also like if your normal run got a 60 and qualifying. And everybody just did normal runs. The guy who drove hard and pushed the limits would blow everybody's doors off. But it's not even possible. Like, yeah, you could do a run that's unbelievable. And it's going to be three points better than the guy who hit all the zones and did everything. So do you I guess like with all that said, what's what is the fix? I mean, a normal run should be a 65. It's just barely passing.
moments.why: Top drivers shred at fun events but play it safe at FD because risk is not rewarded.

Like today was good. To be honest, I feel completely zoned out. I honestly felt like I was just in a flow state and everything was just happening around me. And to be that comfortable in the car is, I'm very proud of that. You know what I mean? Like we're driving at the highest level and to be that relaxed and then to get to battle your friends in the final is absolutely unbelievable. So, yeah, like we were after creating history this year with a one, two, three podium in an event. And now we've done one, two, three in the championship. Like I think I don't know, it's a moment of history and who knows? We could recreate it again next year. But for now, we're after rewriting history and I'm very, very glad to be back to that.
moments.why: Jack eerlijk over zijn spin in de finale

moments.topic: ADAM LZ STEPS AWAY FROM FD
moments.quote: This, uh, this is a little bittersweet for me. So, um, earlier this year, I made the decision that I won't be competing next year in Formula Drift and we've had a rough season and it's been my goal to announce this on the podium. So like I felt so much pressure here because I was like I gotta I gotta do it, right? So yeah, it's it's nothing bad. It's not forever. I'll be coming back at some point but Yeah, I just I wanted this so bad and you know It's not first but I'm really proud to be standing here to get some results for all the fans for my partners Like it's been a rough year, but I'm really happy to be standing here Well, I feel incredibly honored to be one of the first people to receive this information at least publicly I want to thank you so much for everything that you've done for the sport the eyes and the attention and the fans Love you. We've loved having you out here. Thank you so much. I'm sad to see you go, but love to watch you leave You know, I'll be back. I love it here. It's it's a blast. I love driving. I love competing It's just right now. There's some stuff in my life That's a little more important to me and like I want a championship and I got to be fully dedicated to that and I got some Other stuff I got to focus on first

episodes.title: The rise of PERFORMANCE SEDANS… Are 4 doors better than 2?
Rafael Muller aggressive grassroots drifter from Switzerland

moments.quote: Being from Switzerland I found out at Tomodori that you guys do not have any race tracks and motorsports are completely illegal in the country. Well almost yeah like we don't have a race track and circuit racing was forbidden till now. Actually they changed the law this year. No way. Yeah so you could build a race track right now. What we have is like pretty cool hill climbs but like the hill climbs in Switzerland like nothing against them but it's like hard as a normal human you know like it's not easy access to be there. It's like the same old 50 drivers from like 30 years ago which like drive there. But other than that it's I would say yeah hard to do racing like even people who do like motocross they normally go to Italy or like we we go to like France for drifting
moments.why: Swiss drifter explains a country with no race tracks where circuit racing was banned until this year.

moments.quote: Yeah you need to do like a trailer license which is not I mean you just need to do it it's like a driver license but just for the trailer. Then he like back a trailer open stuff. Yeah yeah yeah I think I probably wouldn't have been able to get a trailer license for all. I mean yeah there is like if it's it's it's not hard it's just annoying to do because like you can get like a like a learning permit and you can drive for like two years and then you need to do like the exam and like I mean I drove around Europe with a trailer and like the exam you need to like it matters if you first you know like put the electric part on and then put the like the hitch it's called I feel. Yeah yeah yeah. You know like if you first do the hitch and then the electric part is already like oh no you know. You fail. Yeah you fail.
moments.why: Swiss drifters need a special trailer license, and the exam can be failed on the order of plugging in.

moments.quote: I met him one or two days after I did my driver license randomly on a parking lot he was like shooting pictures of his e36 and I just had my new e30s I was feeling pretty cool you know I had my driver license and shit and he was like oh cool car and I was like yeah tomorrow I install coilovers on it and he was like if you need a hand like let me know and I actually fucked something up like my brake line you know I yeah I just fucked it up and I needed his help and he came over and he was like yeah you say like yesterday that you really like drifting and stuff I'm also interested and I checked last night that there's like a drift event in France should we just like go there and I was like yeah sure like and we went drifting I had my license for like two weeks I mean I didn't knew nothing like I bought the ticket to go drift there and he asked me like do you have an LSD and I was like what is an LSD right he was like yeah let's you know like let's hit that roundabout and I had actually I was lucky I had like OEM LSD with the winter package you know like e36
moments.why: Origin story: two weeks after getting his license he drove seven hours to a French drift day without knowing what an LSD was.

moments.topic: SWISS COILOVERS: 30% MORE AND A TEST
moments.quote: so how it works like you you need to buy kwe like I explained you like imagine you you have a car here you want to install the same idea so you need to see who imports though that brand right so you see ah there's a shop he imports kwe and he will sell you the coilovers for I would say like 30 percent more than they will cost anywhere else because they paid a lot of money to like make them street legal so you buy it with like papers like like a confirmation like okay those coilovers they fit that car and you can drive them so you install them but that's not all after that you need to like go to the inspection center they put it on a lift and they check if you mounted everything right if the right height is good if nothing wraps they go drive the car if something wraps you're walking home you know
moments.why: How street-legal coilovers work in Switzerland: approved brand, import markup, inspection and a test drive.

moments.quote: the cops are like just driving around to search for modified cars wow yeah and that's like that's the hard point because uh what I wanted to say like other countries they maybe have similar rules but it's just like the risk to get caught is less or like a cop will stop you and will be like it's probably illegal but you know like just fucking drive home I give you a warning or whatever which here it's like extremely lucky to like have that yeah like yeah yeah like they're taking your car yeah and it's expensive yeah and you you even like I had a friend he had like basic drift car and he he still had plates on it but the last time he did the inspection was like two years ago and over that time he like did you know basically 36 like no interior anymore like was like swapped it for a 28 and was like 23 on the paper as well as everything he paid like over 10k and lost his license for like two years
moments.why: Swiss police actively hunt modified cars; a friend's drift car cost him over 10k and his license for two years.

moments.topic: A PRINCE IN THE POLAND PADDOCK
moments.quote: and you have cars from everywhere yeah there was a guy like just next to me in a paddock and he shipped his fucking um what was it bent lay full carbon body and he's like a prince of Abu Dhabi like Joel told me probably the richest person you will ever see in your life because you know who it was like yeah and next to it you have like polish guy pumping hard style and super low he's 36 so it's cool like it was a cool like a mixture of drifting we had everything
moments.why: At a huge Polish drift event a full carbon Bentley from Abu Dhabi royalty parked next to a slammed E36 blasting hardstyle.

moments.quote: when this car popped up like how often are there nicely done Silvias that are like legal street legal in Switzerland there are probably just three cars Jans, mine and there's a yellow one I would say who are like in that style street legal but that car I mean I seven years before I bought that car was like yeah almost a kid I texted that guy if you one day sell it let me know yeah and so he's like I'm ready yeah I mean he saved your number no I saw it I saw it for sale I was like I texted him and I sold the M3 I had and everything so sold everything just to buy that car I was like I need that
moments.why: His Silvia is one of only about three street-legal built Silvias in Switzerland, and he waited seven years to buy it.

moments.topic: WHY EURO DRIFT DAYS ARE WET
moments.quote: but the reason why is noise like yeah it's just like less noise and also um most tracks I mean if they have imagine they have like a drift day on dry and like three days afterwards they have like bike racing and it rains and with the rubber like you know like they can't drive so yeah that's why most tracks do like yeah okay we don't like drifting but if we do it we just do it like on wet
moments.why: Explains why so many European tracks only allow drifting on a sprayed wet surface.

moments.quote: the compact also I have it now for like 10 years and the car is fucked like everything is fucked like yeah I have a rule to not spend more than one hour before going drive it like I do a timer the one hour passes I just go as it is and that's the rule it just keeps running I mean it's but is it a 323 ti is it a m42 no it's a m52 oh it swaps no it's original compacts they had six cylinders in here really yeah of course m52 baby
moments.why: His beat-up BMW compact runs on a strict rule: one hour of work max, then it goes on track as is.

moments.quote: it was getting to a point where I where I started not to like it anymore because it felt like a lot of drivers were more driving like demolition derby you know like just get drunk and fucking crash into each other all like they bought like a I don't know like a Volvo for like 200 bucks and they went there drink beers the whole day and just like crashed into each other's and I started to not like that that much but some years after it started to be like people who really drive good like good drivers who drive comp and everything and they were like let's just everyone gets really simple really cheap car we set them up like super grippy with good tires and we just like try to drive as hard as we can without like still driving good you know clean like not crashing for fun into each other and that made it like I had so fucking cool laps there like amazing laps and you're just like you doesn't care like you yeah just like the car is if you know if you total it no one cares that you still don't try to total it
moments.why: A lawless French wet drift event went from drunk demolition derby to good drivers pushing cheap grippy cars.

moments.quote: I did it once like back with the e36 there was like uh was called king of europe and they did like yeah they did like an amateur that's when I started they did like an amateur thing and I was like so hyped you know I was like buying brand new tires with my last money I was like yeah sick and I was not really good but I was not also really bad in that comp right but I felt like man I paid so much to be here and I'm not driving much like this is not fun also the pressure was not really my thing like there I love like the the comp thing about like I want to you know like for me there is nothing cooler that than have people on track who drive way better than I do because that hypes up to like you know like okay cool you know I want to try the same and get better and everyone has like different goals what someone to get more angles someone wants more smoke someone wants to come faster whatever you know like but just like keep pushing to somehow get better for what you love that's important for me otherwise it will get pretty boring
moments.why: A grassroots driver explains why one amateur comp was enough and what really pushes him to get better.

moments.quote: the other thing that I the advice like I don't know where this came from but it was like a way to deal with stress in the moment is think about yourself at like 90 years old yeah that's a good one and how you would feel about getting to relive that moment and try and live that moment from that perspective that's beautiful yeah yeah I don't know because like the desire of being 90 years old and like how much you would romanticize like the shot at getting to like be at a drift event with all your friends and driving again you know like yeah and just know that some point you're gonna be there and like why not enjoy it in that same way
moments.why: Palmer shares a simple mindset trick for enjoying stressful drift days.

moments.quote: they like they don't let you go very fast I don't think you'd enjoy it okay you can drive it it's like it's like a hundred bucks for like a certain amount of laps but like I also I tried to rent it one time and they're like fuck off like you know you're not driving our car I was like what do you mean and they're like no okay but like I think they thought I was gonna because they're like don't go to third is like one of the rules oh really yeah yeah so what's the point that's what I'm saying I was like okay they're like you can't go to third and I was like well then I'm not doing it yeah oh okay no so yeah I mean yeah it'll be fun but you're not going to be able to do the entry I think it but that will be the fun part that's the whole point of the track
moments.why: Palmer on renting a drift car at Ebisu: they told him to get lost, and the rule is no third gear.

moments.quote: I'm really honest I miss to be in a team I love that energy like Dom and kinfe with the s14 we lived in the same apartment for two and a half years and we were just drifting like our apartment was full of tires and spare parts and we had like our living room was just like tree sim rigs so yeah it was like we just lived for that we were like there is just drifting in our life so you really like streeting or like playing sim like yeah like just like and also never no one went somewhere to pick some parts up there was always oh yeah I'm coming I'm coming with you on a Tuesday night we arrived like one in the morning that was not a question you want to come with me it was just like oh yeah let's go you know that was cool we were young
moments.why: Nostalgic story of living with teammates in an apartment full of tires, spare parts and sim rigs.

moments.quote: the most important is like don't push yourself for something that you don't really want for yourself like I'm not talking about having like blowing an engine and that's again like taking the finger out of the asshole and just like okay you need to go through that you'll still love it but like if you feel like to be honest it doesn't give me the same as it used to you don't need to like force yours I see a lot of people I'm like I feel they're done with drifting but they're just doing it because they have nothing else or too much it's become they're like yeah I don't know too much of their identity like yeah yeah personality to be honest I also will have the same like I don't really have that many friends out of drifting stuff like if drifting will be away now will be a pretty empty life
moments.why: Honest take on people who keep drifting out of identity, and admitting his own life would be empty without it.

moments.quote: try not to be hard on people for changing because you don't know what you're gonna be into in front of years because like yeah that's why I was the kid on the internet talking hell of shit about anybody whose car wasn't low yeah and like same calling them a fucking oh you know what I have to you want to be you blah blah blah you know whatever you know what I like now this day today I'm just like fuck what height your car is like I know I was at the I was once the guy was like style over performance you know like if you will like do that interview eight years ago I would say style over performance but now I'm at the point like whatever you know like just having a really good balance yeah yeah yeah it is like it drives really fucking good but also looks really fucking good
moments.why: Both admit they used to roast anyone whose car was not low, and how their view changed.

moments.quote: so my car broke down um I I mean I met Carlos like once quick I think and I text him like dude are you not living near Barcelona I just my car broke down two in the morning was cold that was even was even illegal for me to drive to fucking Spain but I was like fuck it you know yeah um so yeah I texted him and I ended up being there stuck for like two weeks till I got the parts man I had two greats it's one of the greatest two weeks of my life like we went street drifting we drunk beers we're to like a car auction like he he was that time he was like yeah like doing like he's doing like car selling buying stuff it was so good and we ended up to be like really good friends
moments.why: His Land Cruiser died in Spain at 2am and a drifter he barely knew turned it into two of the best weeks of his life.

moments.quote: but imagine you're actually like living here and you go to Spain to drifting and you can't fucking talk to someone there yeah it's like everyone acts like it's okay but I think like it sucks you know it's really fucking sucks it's kind of no one will take out their phone and you know like you know like fucking translate the whole you're just like that's like normal yeah and they stay in their group and we stay in our group and we still have fun you know we laugh you know like you can show emotions but that deep connection is it's hard to get because I think like imagine whole Europe will speak like the same fucking language I think drifting will be on a other point that it is now will be like way more and way more connected and way like we will have something like final about I'm sure because there is a lot of cool shit here just like why not start it's a lot of pressure yeah I yeah I dreamed I think about that yeah I think it's possible
moments.why: Argues that the language barrier keeps European drifting apart, and one language would give Europe its own Final Bout.

moments.quote: who's the French dude with the blue uh s13 mike solvie like yeah he doesn't live that far like he lives not that far from the Swiss border dude that guy ritz and he's like you know so cool but he's like an og yeah he came to super team yeah yeah he was at semashow before yeah and he's like um yeah he drifted comp before with that car like was different of course like with sponsors and shit yeah and yeah I think he drifts for like over 20 years like he's really fucking og of France like he drifts for forever
moments.why: Shout out to an under-the-radar French OG in a blue S13 who has drifted for over 20 years without social media.

moments.quote: and it's so funny like doesn't really matter on like which level of well or like just having money you are like people always spend like everything they have so you have someone with like a hundred k car and he's in the same that someone with a 10k car they are doing the same you know like there's a percentage of income is going yeah it's one has like a 2025 truck with a brand new closed trailer and like a fucking crazy drift car running just like 265s and change them all second lap even if then they have tread on and you have someone who's like but they're doing the same they're like fuck yeah that's cool I never thought about it like that but that's so true yeah yeah just like for the love if you fucking love drifting like yeah you just it's you're spending 50 percent of your income on drifting yeah if not more
moments.why: Whether it's a 100k build or a 10k car, every drifter spends everything they have.

moments.topic: THE NIGHT AT THE JUDGES' TABLE
moments.quote: Final bout like believed in me to be like do you want to be a judge do you want to announce yeah I was like announce I don't think I'd be good at that and they're like I don't know you have a podcast like maybe you could figure it out first year I also not good was the first year the one you did with like I'm sorry I don't know his name the bold guy also really tall guy oh Jimmy Yates yeah yeah yeah but like a r32 yeah skyline yeah you did was that the first year that wasn't the first year okay but I was there when you did that that was fun when was it the year when like front sheet and proceed were going back to back yeah I'm like that was good that was a good year yeah that was really fun and me and Jimmy Yates were like you know and I mean like Raf and me that was the first year we went there mm -hmm and Raf and me we could like I don't know how we ended up there but we were like sitting on the judge table the whole night no and no one kicked us out like everyone was like yeah that was sick that was cool that was really cool that was a cool experience
moments.why: Palmer on becoming a Final Bout announcer, and Rafael sitting at the judges' table all night without being kicked out.

moments.topic: SWISS GUY VS AMERICAN BEER LAWS
moments.quote: I was filming at the entrance with a beer in my hand and the cops showed up and like 10 people were yelling at me like don't drink the beer don't drink the beer and I was like at the door of the cop with my beer and he was like are you the organizer of that event I was like oh no I'm not and they were like put the beer away put the beer away so I was like it's not okay that really happened like that's like a truth so yeah then we anyways I was saying that because like Chicago and it's like Illinois right and uh shawano is like Wisconsin and funny was like we went to like a camping you know like a RV fucking camp place at the lake in shawano and I bought some beers and I asked the lady there like do you have some covers for the beers because everyone told me you need those right and I was like yeah I'm in the US you know like I want to you know I adapt to where I am and she looked at me like what the fuck you want I was like yeah I need to cover the beer and that's three hours from fucking Chicago that's like the next state and she told me like I explained her like yeah I need to cover the beer and then she was like I never heard about that that you need to do that in the US just get your beer
moments.why: A Swiss drifter's confusion about US open container rules, from cops at Final Bout to a Wisconsin campsite.

moments.topic: A JOKE THAT BECAME FINAL BOUT
moments.quote: what would push you to like buy the ticket and go so I was not really doing well right and Raph called me like he was like oh yeah I want to do like a solo trip I was really like not doing well I was like I just need to like leave for a bit and go somewhere else and whatever had some vacations and then he was like just doing as a joke we could go to final bow and I was like I don't know man and then like I called him the next day I was like like you mean serious and he was like yeah it was like two weeks before final bow then we waited like one more week just talking about it and we were like okay let's do it you know and then we bought tickets and we were like oh we need a nesta that's like the document you need to like to come to the US so it was really spontaneous yeah just was like a fuck it let's do it thing yeah and yeah he was like struggling to like afford it and I think like his dad landed him some money he was like you know what like you're in your mid -20s you should experience that once I give you some money you pay me back and shit
moments.why: A rough year, a joke phone call and two weeks later two Europeans were on their way to Final Bout.

moments.quote: that's why the environment's important that's why I like going to people because it's like this is your space you know you can like tell your story in your space you know feels like therapy yeah a little bit that's my goal yeah I've actually been thinking about like going to school to be a therapist lately really yeah actually haven't said that brand new infos yeah we'll see I don't have a lot of but I think I care a lot about that I'm like helping people
moments.why: The Goodest Cast host drops brand new info: he's thinking about studying to become a therapist.

episodes.title: LB2 Pro Podium

moments.guest: JAMES DEANE, JACK SHANAHAN, ADAM LZ
moments.quote: We met him at the BGS one night, and I was walking up, he just swings around, he's like what's the crack, lad? And I was like, what the hell is going on? He said it nowhere. What's your favourite one? Are we going there anyway? No, you just add anyway then at the end of stuff. Anyway then. They'll just say something and at the end it's like anyway then. So we're gonna do the podcast anyway then.
moments.why: Adam LZ greeting the Irish drivers with their own slang is a fun bit of paddock chemistry.

moments.guest: JAMES DEANE, JACK SHANAHAN, ADAM LZ
moments.quote: Especially when the sun goes down, we don't get any practice. Usually our qualifying laps are the first time we drive in a dark and all your reference points change. But I feel like FD did a really good job here in Long Beach too to light the track in the correct areas. It's the first time all year by the way. Yeah, so you're getting better. Yeah, so improvement. Remember what you did and do it again. I was a bit worried on the last corner because the smoke was such an issue before that. I was like, oh at night it's going to be terrible. But I guess they put fans in. It was never an issue for me. And there was a bit of a wind tonight as well. I checked the weather this morning. I'm like, what's the wind in the evening? And it was I think 8 miles per hour. I think we got that helping us too.
moments.why: Drivers reveal their first laps in the dark were qualifying laps, with all reference points changed.

moments.guest: JAMES DEANE, JACK SHANAHAN, ADAM LZ
moments.topic: NO SMOKING AT A DRIFT EVENT
moments.quote: Maybe next year, if we come back here and it's a really still day, no wind, they need to maybe put a banner between that outside zone fight, like a big flag banner. Let the smoke come all the way up. I like the wall, like one of the barriers for the wall. They put a barrier there and a big banner, like FD. Yeah, it helps. Stop the smoke. No smoking here. It is up in the tower in the booth. There's no smoking signs everywhere and it's just like, it makes me giggle every time I see it. It's a big plume comes in like, right, yeah, no smoking.
moments.why: The podium jokes about the no smoking signs in a tower full of tire smoke, and pitches a smoke banner.

moments.quote: My off season doesn't start until December. Yeah, you have some stuff on the go. I had no further China for some stuff. Quite busy. Next weekend we go to IDS. I'm a running car there, so I'll be working as a mechanic. Oh, cool. And then the week after we go to China. Then the week after we go to Japan. Week after we go to Cyprus. And then the week after that we do a rally. And then the week after that I might take over your holidays. You should. Yeah, you should. And then we're on the off for the first or only after three weeks in December. And then we go straight to Oman, Virginia again. It's just all go, to be honest. But look, MayK is the sun shines, you know? So that's kind of where we're at. Just keep going. I like the little grin Adam kind of was throwing on there with like hearing that busy schedule and kind of knowing you're like, I'm starting to pull away a little bit. Like that sounds crazy. It's a lot, but I mean, look, if you want to be the best driver, you drive as much as you can. Yeah, exactly. Yeah, that's kind of where I'm at. I'm just like, you know, all the events that I'm offered to do, I'm like, I may as well go and just build experience of different drivers, different tracks and just keep getting better, you know?
moments.why: Jack Shanahan lists a packed off season: IDS, China, Japan, Cyprus, a rally and more.

moments.topic: ADAM LZ PLANNED HIS PODIUM GOODBYE
moments.quote: Adam, obviously you announced, taking a step back for a bit. I do love that you put in like, I am coming back. I just need this break. Can I ask when that moment happened where you said, hey, this is... I got to do something else? Yeah, that's a good question. Probably earlier this year. But I was like, I was dead set. I was like, I'm not going to... I don't want to do it like right before next season, right? I was like, it's got to be on the podium. And this is like, this is the last chance I had at that. Adam said it to me earlier. He's like, I don't know, top 16 or something. And I said, are you coming back next year and you told me and you said, yeah, I'm going to announce it on the podium. And I just wished him that. That is fucking cool. I like that. I like that. He did it.
moments.why: Adam LZ reveals he wanted to announce his step back only from the podium, and Jack knew in advance.

moments.topic: ADAM LZ'S PRO CAR: NEW PLANS?
moments.quote: Question that I guess about the car. Are you just going to park the pro car or just turn into a party car at this point? I've got some plans for it. Like non -drift related plans. It was like fun ideas that I've never done because I'm always like I can't hurt the car because of the race season. So like I don't want to spoil too much. But it's like a couple of them will happen in the next couple months. So I'm excited. The car made it back in one piece. That's great. So I'm guessing you're turning the boost all the way up. You're gripping it up to the max. Oh no, better than that. Really? Yeah. Different disciplines of motorsport.
moments.why: Adam LZ teases non-drift plans for his Pro car during his break.

moments.topic: JACK SHANAHAN: NEW CAR IN 4 WEEKS
moments.quote: Yeah, I guess it was pretty good, to be honest. Turned over all. Yeah, pretty good. To be honest, I didn't expect to be this far in the championship. At the start of the year, we obviously had quite a big issues in Long Beach. We still ended up in the podium. And then we kind of carried the momentum through the season. moments.topic: OFF-SEASON: NORWAY, ICE AND NEW WIRING
moments.quote: I'm, uh, like last year, I don't know if you, if you know, if you knew, but I went to Norway for, uh, ice drifting and it was really, really fun. Um, very cool. So I definitely want to try to go back again because, uh, that was, uh, that was a fun experience. And for sure, I'm going to also set up my three fifties that I have at home for ice drifting. So it's going to be mainly the, uh, the, the big project for the, uh, for the drifting and the off season. And after that, well, the Corvette is going to be as, uh, like his second season since we build it. So I'm probably going to change the whole wiring on the car just cause it has a lot of beating. And also we had a, uh, not a big fire, but a considerate, uh, good fire during the DMCC round, uh, back in Quebec here. So, uh, yeah, I think it would be wise to just put in a fresh, uh, set of wiring on the, on the car.
moments.why: Off-season plans: Norway ice drifting again and new wiring after a fire at a DMCC round.

moments.topic: WHY THE CORVETTE MAKES TINY MISTAKES LOOK BIG
moments.quote: I'm always comparing it with the S chassis, but I'm not trying to make the car drive like the S chassis because I know this car is way more sensitive, uh, or we can see twitchy, but also has a ton of front grip, which the S chassis was always lacking of. So like, I definitely don't want the Corvette to handle like the S S C. I just want to reduce the, uh, the, the, the things that are looking bad with the Corvette, which is always a small correction. They look so big because everything looks like everything looks more with the Corvette. So if you do something very good, it's going to look very good. Also, if you do a very tiny correction, it's also going to look big. And that's the main thing I'm focusing on to, uh, to get rid of for sure.
moments.why: Corvette has more front grip than his old S chassis but every small correction looks huge.

moments.topic: HIS ORANGE DEMO CAR IS 700 LBS HEAVIER
moments.quote: let me go back to my practice car, you know, my demo car that I brought at the world tour, which is now orange. Well, this car doesn't drive at all like my competition car. And some people that are not very deep into a drifting, sometimes they think it's the same car, you know, they're like, Oh, you brought your racing car or you change your living room, your car. Like, no, no, it's different. And it's like, you know, it's like a Miura and a, a, a Sauer. It's like two completely different car cause one, one, uh, weighs 2900 pounds. And the other one, the practice car weighs 3 ,600 pounds. So right there, there's a huge difference. And the weight distribution is like 5% different front to rear with the competition car. So all of that makes the car handles really, really differently.
moments.why: Fans think his orange demo car is his FD car. It is 3,600 lb versus 2,900 lb for the competition car.

moments.topic: GREY WHEELS AND BLACK GLOVES HIDE CORRECTIONS
moments.quote: Well, this, I made a decision, uh, quite some time ago to go with everything that's going to help me, uh, more than something that that's going to be more stylish. Back in the days, I, I was more like, okay, let's go white whales. Let's go with this and that, but being in pro, I feel that every little things that can help, help me, I will use it for me. So now I'm, uh, not black wheels, but it's a gray wheels. So you don't really see lots of the correction. Well, you see less correction than with white wheels for sure. Same things for my gloves. My gloves. Now I'm only using black gloves back in prospect when I won a championship in 24, I like a fluoro or a yellow gloves, which is like, you know, it's, it's cool. It's nice legs, but maybe not the wise, wise, the smooth to do when you want to, uh, you know, go under the radar with your correction.
moments.why: He switched from white wheels and fluo gloves to grey wheels and black gloves so judges see less correction.

moments.quote: Oh, I've been asked this question a couple of times last weekend. And, uh, I think it's, too big of a statement, you know, maybe it's, it's a bit too much. And we were laughing about it, but we were like, for sure there will be some like complaints, you know, like it's too, it's too bright, you know, like with, for my eyes or something like that.
moments.why: Fans asked if the glowing orange demo livery comes to FD. Fun, short.

moments.topic: DOES A WHITE CAR CAUSE MORE CRASHES?
moments.quote: I know. We'll probably talk about hockey a few times, but like in the NHL, goalie started swapping to white pads to increase their save percentage. And there was a direct correlation between having white goalie pads because players look for a white when they go to shoot, because they think it's the back of the net. So I'm like, Hmm, I wonder if not that like a driver would want more accidents, but like you might cause more mistakes in the chase by having a white car.
moments.why: NHL goalies went to white pads to fool shooters; would an all-white drift car do the same to chase drivers?

moments.topic: C7 VS C6: NOT JUST A RESHELL
moments.quote: I didn't realize the, I know very little about Corvette platform. So forgive my ignorance, but I didn't realize there was that big of a difference between the C six and the C seven. I thought it was like kind of just a re shelled. Hey, here's a, an updated look. Yeah. And I see that's what I thought at first. And I got into it and you're like, Oh, no, exactly. Like just said, told me when I started the project, he was like, you should just build a C six and put a C seven buddy kit on it. And it was like, hell no, I don't want to do this, but now I'm thinking about it. I'm like, maybe that would have been a good idea. You know, like a C six point five. Yeah. I like that. I like that. But, um, yeah, there is some difference, but also the whole chassis is aluminum. The subframes on aluminum, which is not the same in the, the C six platform. So it looks the same, but it is quite different. And then the rigidity, the rigidity of the chassis is like 30% more than the C six.
moments.why: The C7 chassis is aluminium with aluminium subframes and about 30 percent stiffer than the C6.

moments.quote: I think it was, it was a great challenge cause a lot of people, maybe like 80% of the talk to me about that were like, uh, he tried it first and it was not a very, uh, it wasn't a success. So why are you trying it? Like you're gonna, you know, you're gonna lose your time. It's not gonna work. You're gonna fail blah, blah, blah. And I kind of took it as a, you know, like I dare you, you know, a challenge.
moments.why: Most people told him the C7 would fail because the first one struggled. He took it as a dare.

moments.topic: WHY HE PICKED A C7 OVER A C6
moments.quote: that's also one of the reason why I went with the C seven because I knew that if I started right at the best with a C six, well, companies already developed the products around this car. And for me, it makes me less attractive, let's say, as a driver, as a sponsor driver. So I wanted to go with the C seven just to make sure I'm, I'm offering something completely different. The company is a new product to put on the market and you think develop. And that's exactly what we did.
moments.why: A C6 already had all the parts. A C7 gave sponsors a new product to develop and sell.

moments.quote: Well, thing is last year was probably my worst, uh, financial season, uh, so far, because we did blew up, uh, three engines during the season and one right before we started in Long Beach, one and one at the event. So yeah, basically it costs a lot. So this year, even with the, the, the exchange rate with the fuel and everything based in the, in US and Canada, it's still going to be way less expensive than last year, which is a good news. And, uh, which helps me to, uh, you know, breathe a bit more because last year was really hard on the budget. And this year, I feel like it's all right. It's, it's making sense. It's how I planned it.
moments.why: Last season he blew three engines; this year is cheaper even with the exchange rate.

moments.topic: SAVING RACE FUEL TO GET HOME
moments.quote: for us, we heard the news and we were like, are we going to be able to push you in the truck, you know, to go from west to east? Cause there is some gas station where there is no more fuel and DSL for whatever political reason, you know? So we were like, all right, maybe we're going to have to empty my, uh, my VP racing fuel jug that we use in the Corvette at the race, keep it in the trailer and make some reserve to be able to go back home at the end of the season.
moments.why: The Canadian team planned to keep race fuel in the trailer in case diesel ran out on the drive home.

moments.topic: HE COPIED ANOTHER DRIVER'S STEERING WHEEL
moments.quote: Something that we, uh, we changed and, uh, I never thought I had, I was going to change that for this. It's my steering wheel. We put a big, a bigger steering wheel and we already had the idea in our mind, but when we saw a rat down with his Supra with this, we were like, Oh, okay. So I texted him and I was like, Hey, Dan, I need, I need the same steering that you run. And, uh, now we run the same steering wheel in FD.
moments.why: Saw a Supra driver with a bigger wheel, texted him, now runs the same one. Driver name unclear in transcript.

moments.topic: ICE DRIFTING ALMOST AS FAST AS ASPHALT
moments.quote: And in the winter, it's really cool cause we have big stud studded tires and we can go on ice and be almost as fast. Well, it depends on the study, but I have some stuff that are faster than on the asphalt. So, but it just makes the ice go down so quickly. So I don't really put them often unless it's a demo or something like that. But when I do the drift academy, I have 60 millimeters studs, um, which is a bit like the guys from Norway are using it over there. So it makes the car really fast and you can keep the same set of tire for the whole day.
moments.why: Studded tires on ice can be faster than asphalt; one set lasts a whole day.

moments.topic: RACE DRIVERS LEARN TO DRIFT ON ICE
moments.quote: So last winter I had, uh, maybe four drivers from the front series. So two drivers that were doing, uh, formula 2000 in the U S and, uh, some drivers that were doing NASCAR and one driver that was doing, uh, like, uh, you know, the, the Mi-Mikha cup or like the, the Nisaka challenge, which is like 400 Z's. Um, but, uh, racing and they did it just so they can understand more the handling of the car. So when they go racing, they understand when they are at the limit of the, of the car, you know, cause some of the racing people, they, they never experienced real fly and real drifting, you know? So when you know, and you're comfortable with this section of racing or motor sport, well, you're, you're also more confident in your own section of motor sports, which is great racing.
moments.why: Formula 2000 and NASCAR drivers come to his ice school to learn car control at the limit.

moments.quote: Uh, I don't think so, man. Cause it's funny cause it right. Well now it's October 12th, but tomorrow is my birthday. So, uh, this weekend my girlfriend brought me to, um, how do you call this in English? When you, you jumped from the plane and you, you opened skydiving. Okay. Skydiving. Yeah. So I want skydiving this past weekend. Yeah. I want skydiving, uh, two days ago and it was my first time and I was, I was calm and I was, I was so calm before. And it was awesome, but like, I, like almost, well I got enough adrenaline, but I will say like, I, when I do a really nice chase, I get the same amount of adrenaline than that.
